title: Feeding the Hearth
sceneText:
In the afternoon someone comes to say that there is a Forge-keeper waiting for you at the forge-chapel.

You have never been into that room. It is at the end of the west wing of the main house, a small stone room with a stone hearth set into the middle of the floor, the fire burning very low and very steady. The air smells of old smoke and cold stone.

A man in his fifties is crouched at the edge of the hearth, putting wood in. He does it slowly, one piece at a time, waiting a little after each.

“Lorenz.” He does not get up. “I keep three estates in this part of the valley.”

He puts in the last piece, watches the fire gather again, and only then stands and brushes the ash off his hands.

“Every time a stewardship changes hands I come and feed it once. There is nothing particular in it. It is so the hearth knows there has been a change.”

Having said that, he starts for the door, and stops halfway.

“Somebody feeds this hearth every day, so it stays alive. If nobody comes, it goes cold.”

He looks at you once. “I am not saying you have to come every day. I am saying the room is here.”

He pushes the door open, and then remembers something.

“Also: I keep the vigil here on Thursday nights.”

“Keep the vigil over what?”

“Over nothing,” he says. “I sit, and I watch the fire into the small hours.”

“It is a matter of practice. Not a large matter of practice. The three estates’ forge-chapels take it in turn, and Maplegate has Thursdays.”

Before he pulls the door to he adds one last thing.

“If you have nothing else on that night, you can come and sit. Or not.”
